questions.question: A student scored 456 marks out of 600. What percentage of the total marks did the student score?
questions.subject: Percentages
questions.explanation: Percentage = (Marks obtained / Total marks) x 100 = (456 / 600) x 100 = 76%.

questions.question: In a college of 1,200 students, 45% are girls. How many boys are there?
questions.subject: Percentages

questions.question: The price of an article increases from Rs 800 to Rs 920. Find the percentage increase.
questions.subject: Percentages
questions.explanation: Increase = 920 - 800 = 120. Percentage increase = (120 / 800) x 100 = 15%.

questions.question: A number is increased by 20% and then the result is decreased by 20%. What is the net percentage change?
questions.subject: Percentages
questions.explanation: Net factor = 1.20 x 0.80 = 0.96, i.e. 96% of the original, a net 4% decrease.

questions.question: If 30% of a number is 84, what is 45% of the same number?
questions.subject: Percentages

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys an article for Rs 450 and sells it for Rs 540. Find the profit percentage.
questions.subject: Profit and Loss

questions.question: By selling a watch for Rs 1,800, a man incurs a loss of 10%. Find the cost price of the watch.
questions.subject: Profit and Loss
questions.explanation: SP = CP x (1 - Loss%). So 1800 = CP x 0.90, giving CP = 1800 / 0.90 = Rs 2,000.

questions.question: A trader marks his goods 20% above the cost price and then allows a discount of 10%. What is his profit percentage?
questions.subject: Profit and Loss

questions.question: A man sells two articles for Rs 990 each. On one he gains 10% and on the other he loses 10%. What is his overall result?
questions.subject: Profit and Loss
questions.explanation: For equal SP with equal gain/loss %, the seller always incurs a net loss of about R^2/100 = 100/100 = 1%, i.e. a 1% loss.

questions.question: The cost price of 12 articles equals the selling price of 10 articles. Find the profit percentage.
questions.subject: Profit and Loss
questions.explanation: CP x 12 = SP x 10, so SP/CP = 12/10 = 1.2, giving a profit of 20%.

questions.question: A can complete a job in 12 days and B can complete it in 18 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
questions.subject: Time and Work
questions.explanation: One day work = 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36. Time = 36/5 = 7.2 days.

questions.question: A and B together can finish a work in 6 days. A alone can finish it in 10 days. In how many days can B alone finish it?
questions.subject: Time and Work
questions.explanation: B's one day work = 1/6 - 1/10 = 1/15, so B alone takes 15 days.

questions.question: If 8 workers can build a wall in 12 days, how many days will 6 workers take to build the same wall at the same rate?
questions.subject: Time and Work
questions.explanation: Work is constant: 8 x 12 = 6 x d, so d = 96 / 6 = 16 days.

questions.question: Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours, pipe B in 8 hours, and pipe C empties it in 12 hours. If all three are opened together, in how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.subject: Time and Work

questions.question: A is twice as efficient as B. Working together they finish a job in 8 days. In how many days can B alone finish it?
questions.subject: Time and Work
questions.explanation: Let B's rate = x, A's rate = 2x. Combined = 3x, so total work = 8 x 3x = 24x. B alone = 24x / x = 24 days.

questions.question: A train covers 360 km in 4 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.subject: Time Speed Distance
questions.explanation: Speed = Distance / Time = 360 / 4 = 90 km/h.

questions.question: A car travels 150 km from A to B at 60 km/h and returns at 50 km/h. What is the average speed for the whole journey?
questions.subject: Time Speed Distance

questions.question: A man walking at 5 km/h reaches his office 10 minutes late. If he walks at 6 km/h, he reaches 5 minutes early. Find the distance to his office.
questions.subject: Time Speed Distance
questions.explanation: Time difference = 15 min = 0.25 h. d/5 - d/6 = 0.25, so d(1/30) = 0.25, giving d = 7.5 km.

questions.question: A train 150 m long passes a pole in 15 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.subject: Time Speed Distance

questions.question: A boat covers 24 km downstream in 2 hours. If the speed of the stream is 2 km/h, find the speed of the boat in still water.
questions.subject: Time Speed Distance
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 24/2 = 12 km/h. Boat + stream = 12, so boat = 12 - 2 = 10 km/h.

questions.question: Find the simple interest on Rs 5,000 at 8% per annum for 3 years.
questions.subject: Simple Interest

questions.question: In what time will Rs 4,000 yield a simple interest of Rs 720 at 6% per annum?
questions.subject: Simple Interest
questions.explanation: 720 = (4000 x 6 x T)/100, so 720 = 240T, giving T = 3 years.

questions.question: At what rate per annum will Rs 2,500 amount to Rs 3,100 in 3 years at simple interest?
questions.subject: Simple Interest

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum for 5 years at 7% per annum is Rs 1,750. Find the sum.
questions.subject: Simple Interest

questions.question: Find the compound interest on Rs 8,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually.
questions.subject: Compound Interest

questions.question: Find the difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on Rs 5,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum.
questions.subject: Compound Interest

questions.question: What will Rs 10,000 amount to in 2 years at 20% per annum compound interest, compounded annually?
questions.subject: Compound Interest

questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself in 5 years at compound interest. In how many years will it become 4 times itself?
questions.subject: Compound Interest
questions.explanation: Doubling twice gives 4 times, so the time is 2 x 5 = 10 years.

questions.question: Rs 1,200 is divided between A and B in the ratio 3 : 5. How much does A receive?
questions.subject: Ratios and Proportions

questions.question: If a : b = 2 : 3 and b : c = 4 : 5, find a : c.
questions.subject: Ratios and Proportions

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 5 : 7 and their sum is 144. Find the larger number.
questions.subject: Ratios and Proportions
questions.explanation: Larger number = (7/12) x 144 = 84.

questions.question: A mixture of 40 litres contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. How much water must be added so that the ratio of milk to water becomes 3 : 2?
questions.subject: Ratios and Proportions
questions.explanation: Milk = 30 L, water = 10 L. For 30 : w = 3 : 2, w = 20. Add 20 - 10 = 10 litres.

questions.question: The average of 5 numbers is 18. If one of the numbers, 25, is removed, what is the average of the remaining numbers?
questions.subject: Averages
questions.explanation: Sum of 5 = 90. Remaining sum = 90 - 25 = 65. Average = 65/4 = 16.25.

questions.question: The average age of 20 students is 15 years. When the teacher's age is included, the average becomes 16 years. Find the teacher's age.
questions.subject: Averages
questions.explanation: New total = 21 x 16 = 336. Old total = 20 x 15 = 300. Teacher = 336 - 300 = 36 years.

questions.question: Find the average of the first 10 natural numbers.
questions.subject: Averages

questions.question: Find the HCF of 72 and 120.
questions.subject: Number Systems

questions.question: Find the LCM of 12, 15 and 20.
questions.subject: Number Systems

questions.question: What is the unit digit of 7 raised to the power 45?
questions.subject: Number Systems
questions.explanation: Powers of 7 cycle 7, 9, 3, 1 with period 4. 45 mod 4 = 1, so the unit digit is 7.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 3 raised to the power 100 is divided by 5?
questions.subject: Number Systems
questions.explanation: 3^4 = 81 is congruent to 1 mod 5. Since 100 = 4 x 25, 3^100 = (3^4)^25 is congruent to 1 mod 5. Remainder = 1.

questions.question: If x + 1/x = 5, find the value of x^2 + 1/x^2.
questions.subject: Algebra

questions.question: If 2x + 3y = 12 and x - y = 1, find the value of x.
questions.subject: Algebra

questions.question: Find the area of a triangle whose base is 14 cm and height is 9 cm.
questions.subject: Geometry
questions.explanation: Area = 1/2 x base x height = 1/2 x 14 x 9 = 63 cm^2.

questions.question: Find the circumference of a circle of radius 7 cm. (Take pi = 22/7)
questions.subject: Geometry
questions.explanation: Circumference = 2 x pi x r = 2 x (22/7) x 7 = 44 cm.

questions.question: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. Find the largest angle.
questions.subject: Geometry
questions.explanation: Sum = 9 parts = 180 degrees, so 1 part = 20 degrees. Largest = 4 x 20 = 80 degrees.

questions.question: Find the length of the diagonal of a square whose side is 10 cm.
questions.subject: Geometry
questions.explanation: Diagonal = side x sqrt(2) = 10 sqrt(2) cm.

questions.question: The table shows the number of units sold by a company in four quarters: Q1 = 240, Q2 = 300, Q3 = 280, Q4 = 380. What is the average number of units sold per quarter?
questions.subject: Data Interpretation

questions.question: A company's revenue was Rs 5.0 crore in 2022 and Rs 6.5 crore in 2023. What is the percentage increase in revenue?
questions.subject: Data Interpretation
questions.explanation: Increase = 1.5 crore. Percentage increase = (1.5 / 5.0) x 100 = 30%.

questions.question: In a survey of 500 employees, 55% preferred option A and the rest preferred option B. If 40% of those who preferred option A were from the IT department, how many IT employees preferred option A?
questions.subject: Data Interpretation
questions.explanation: Option A = 55% of 500 = 275. IT share = 40% of 275 = 110.

questions.question: Find the next number in the series: 4, 9, 19, 39, 79, ?
questions.subject: Number Series

questions.question: Find the next number in the series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.subject: Number Series
questions.explanation: The terms are n(n+1): 1x2, 2x3, 3x4, 4x5, 5x6, 6x7 = 42.

questions.question: Find the next number in the series: 3, 7, 16, 35, 74, ?
questions.subject: Number Series
questions.explanation: Multiply by 2 and add an increasing number: x2+1, x2+2, x2+3, x2+4, x2+5. So 74 x 2 + 5 = 153.

questions.question: Find the next number in the series: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ?
questions.subject: Number Series
questions.explanation: These are perfect squares: 1^2, 2^2, 3^2, 4^2, 5^2, 6^2 = 36.

questions.question: Find the next number in the series: 5, 11, 23, 47, 95, ?
questions.subject: Number Series

questions.question: Find the next number in the series: 120, 99, 80, 63, 48, ?
questions.subject: Number Series
questions.explanation: Differences are 21, 19, 17, 15, and next 13. So 48 - 13 = 35.

questions.question: Find the next letter in the series: A, C, F, J, O, ?
questions.subject: Letter Series

questions.question: Find the next letter in the series: Z, X, U, Q, L, ?
questions.subject: Letter Series
questions.explanation: Subtract 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 letters: Z->X, X->U, U->Q, Q->L, L->F.

questions.question: Find the next term in the series: AZ, BY, CX, ?
questions.subject: Letter Series
questions.explanation: First letters A, B, C, D; second letters Z, Y, X, W. So the next term is DW.

questions.question: Find the next letter in the series: A, B, D, G, K, ?
questions.subject: Letter Series
questions.explanation: Add 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 letters: A->B, B->D, D->G, G->K, K->P.

questions.question: If CAT is coded as 3120 (using A = 1, B = 2, ... Z = 26), how is DOG coded?
questions.subject: Coding-Decoding
questions.explanation: DOG: D = 4, O = 15, G = 7, so the code is 4157.

questions.question: In a certain code, PEN is written as QFO. How is INK written in the same code?
questions.subject: Coding-Decoding
questions.explanation: Each letter moves forward by 1: I->J, N->O, K->L, giving JOL.

questions.question: If FRIEND is coded as HTKGPF (each letter shifted forward by 2), how is CANDLE coded?
questions.subject: Coding-Decoding
questions.explanation: Shift each letter of CANDLE forward by 2: C->E, A->C, N->P, D->F, L->N, E->G = ECPFNG.

questions.question: In a code, TERM is written as UFTN. Using the same rule, how is EXAM written?
questions.subject: Coding-Decoding
questions.explanation: Each letter moves forward by 1: E->F, X->Y, A->B, M->N, giving FYBN.

questions.question: A man walks 5 km towards the north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 5 km. How far is he from the starting point and in which direction?
questions.subject: Direction Sense
questions.explanation: Moving 5 km north and then 5 km south cancels out, leaving a net displacement of 3 km to the east.

questions.question: Ravi walks 6 km towards the east and then 8 km towards the north. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.subject: Direction Sense
questions.explanation: Distance = sqrt(6^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(100) = 10 km.

questions.question: A person starts facing north. He turns 90 degrees to the left, then 90 degrees to the left again, then 90 degrees to the right. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.subject: Direction Sense
questions.explanation: North -> (left) West -> (left) South -> (right) West. He is facing west.

questions.question: A man faces the rising sun, turns 90 degrees to his right and then turns 180 degrees. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.subject: Direction Sense
questions.explanation: Facing east -> right gives south -> 180 degrees gives north.

questions.question: Pointing to a photograph, a man says, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is the girl related to the man?
questions.subject: Blood Relations
questions.explanation: Grandfather's only son is the man's father. The father's daughter is the man's sister.

questions.question: A is B's brother, B is C's father, and C is D's sister. How is A related to D?
questions.subject: Blood Relations
questions.explanation: A is the brother of B, who is D's father. So A is D's uncle.

questions.question: If P + Q means 'P is the mother of Q' and P - Q means 'P is the brother of Q', how is A related to C in 'A + B - C'?
questions.subject: Blood Relations
questions.explanation: A is B's mother and B is C's brother, so A is also C's mother.

questions.question: Introducing a man, a woman said, 'His wife is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the man related to the woman?
questions.subject: Blood Relations
questions.explanation: The only daughter of the woman's mother is the woman herself, so the man's wife is the woman, making the man her husband.

questions.question: Statements: All roses are flowers. All flowers are plants. Conclusions: I. All roses are plants. II. All plants are roses.
questions.subject: Syllogisms
questions.explanation: All roses are flowers and all flowers are plants, so all roses are plants (I follows). II reverses the relation and is not valid.

questions.question: Statements: Some pens are books. All books are pencils. Conclusions: I. Some pens are pencils. II. All pencils are books.
questions.subject: Syllogisms
questions.explanation: Some pens are books and all books are pencils, so some pens are pencils (I follows). II is not a valid converse.

questions.question: Statements: All engineers are graduates. Some graduates are managers. Conclusions: I. Some engineers are managers. II. Some managers are graduates.
questions.subject: Syllogisms
questions.explanation: From 'some graduates are managers', the converse 'some managers are graduates' (II) follows. I does not necessarily follow.

questions.question: Statements: No cat is a dog. All dogs are animals. Conclusions: I. No cat is an animal. II. Some animals are dogs.
questions.subject: Syllogisms
questions.explanation: All dogs are animals, so some animals are dogs (II follows). I is not valid, since cats could still be animals.

questions.question: Five friends P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing north. R is at the extreme left. T is at the extreme right. Q is immediately to the right of R. S is not adjacent to T. Who sits in the middle?
questions.subject: Seating Arrangements
questions.explanation: Position 1 = R, 2 = Q, 5 = T. S is not adjacent to T, so S is at position 3 and P at position 4. The middle seat (position 3) is S.

questions.question: Five colleagues A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing north. B is at the extreme left. D is at the extreme right. C sits exactly in the middle. A is an immediate neighbour of B. Who sits second to the right of A?
questions.subject: Seating Arrangements
questions.explanation: Position 1 = B, 3 = C, 5 = D. A is an immediate neighbour of B, so A is at position 2 and E at position 4. Second to the right of A (position 2) is position 4 = E.

questions.question: Six persons A, B, C, D, E and F sit in a row facing north. D is at the extreme left and F at the extreme right. A is immediately to the right of D. E is immediately to the left of F. C is not next to A. Who sits at the third position from the left?
questions.subject: Seating Arrangements
questions.explanation: Positions: 1 = D, 2 = A, 5 = E, 6 = F. B and C occupy positions 3 and 4. Since C is not next to A (position 2), C is at 4 and B is at 3.

questions.question: If by a certain code BOOK = 43 and PEN = 35 (where each letter is replaced by its position in the alphabet, A = 1), what is the value of CAP?
questions.subject: Logical Puzzles

questions.question: Five boxes are stacked one above another. P is immediately above Q, R is immediately above P, S is at the bottom, and T is above R. Which box is immediately above Q?
questions.subject: Logical Puzzles
questions.explanation: From top to bottom: T, R, P, Q, S. The box immediately above Q is P.

questions.question: In a group of 40 students, 25 play cricket and 20 play football. If every student plays at least one of the two games, how many students play both games?
questions.subject: Logical Puzzles

questions.question: In a family of three children, every child has at least one sister. What is the minimum number of girls in the family?
questions.subject: Logical Puzzles
questions.explanation: With one girl and two boys, the girl would have no sister. With two girls and one boy, each girl has the other as a sister and the boy has sisters. So the minimum is 2.

questions.question: What is the value of x? Statement I: 2x + 3 = 11. Statement II: x is a positive integer.
questions.option4: Even together, the statements are not sufficient
questions.subject: Data Sufficiency
questions.explanation: Statement I gives x = 4 uniquely, so I alone is sufficient. Statement II alone does not determine a single value.

questions.question: Is the number n divisible by 6? Statement I: n is divisible by 3. Statement II: n is even.
questions.option4: Even together, the statements are not sufficient
questions.subject: Data Sufficiency
questions.explanation: A number divisible by both 3 and 2 is divisible by 6. Neither statement alone is enough, but both together are sufficient.

questions.question: All managers in a company have laptops. Some employees with laptops work from home. Which of the following must be true?
questions.option3: All employees with laptops are managers
questions.subject: Deductive Logic
questions.explanation: The statements do not guarantee that any manager works from home, nor that all laptop holders are managers. None of the given conclusions is forced.

questions.question: If A means '+', B means '-', and C means 'x', find the value of 12 A 4 B 3.
questions.subject: Deductive Logic

questions.question: Statement: If it rains, the match will be cancelled. It did not rain. Which conclusion follows?
questions.option1: The match will definitely be played
questions.option2: The match will definitely be cancelled
questions.option3: The match may or may not be cancelled
questions.answer: The match may or may not be cancelled
questions.subject: Deductive Logic
questions.explanation: The given condition only links rain to cancellation. Since it did not rain, nothing definite can be concluded about the match.

questions.question: Choose the word most similar in meaning to ABUNDANT.
questions.subject: Synonyms
questions.explanation: Abundant means existing in large quantities, i.e. plentiful.

questions.question: Choose the word most similar in meaning to DILIGENT.
questions.subject: Synonyms
questions.explanation: Diligent means showing careful and persistent effort, i.e. hardworking.

questions.question: Choose the word most similar in meaning to CANDID.

questions.explanation: Candid means truthful and straightforward, i.e. frank.

questions.question: Choose the word most similar in meaning to LUCID.
questions.subject: Synonyms
questions.explanation: Lucid means expressed clearly and easy to understand.

questions.question: Choose the word most similar in meaning to MITIGATE.
questions.subject: Synonyms
questions.explanation: Mitigate means to make less severe or painful, i.e. alleviate.

questions.question: Choose the word most similar in meaning to METICULOUS.
questions.subject: Synonyms
questions.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail, i.e. very careful.

questions.question: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to EPHEMERAL.
questions.subject: Antonyms
questions.explanation: Ephemeral means short-lived, so its opposite is permanent.

questions.question: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to BENEVOLENT.
questions.subject: Antonyms
questions.explanation: Benevolent means kind and well-meaning, so its opposite is cruel.

questions.question: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to SCARCITY.
questions.subject: Antonyms
questions.explanation: Scarcity means shortage, so its opposite is abundance.

questions.question: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to OBSOLETE.
questions.subject: Antonyms
questions.explanation: Obsolete means no longer in use, so its opposite is modern.

questions.question: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to FRUGAL.
questions.subject: Antonyms
questions.explanation: Frugal means economical, so its opposite is extravagant.

questions.question: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to HUMBLE.
questions.subject: Antonyms
questions.explanation: Humble means modest, so its opposite is arrogant.

questions.question: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error: Each of the students (A) / have submitted (B) / their assignments (C) / on time. (D)
questions.subject: Error Identification
questions.explanation: The subject 'Each' is singular, so 'have submitted' should be 'has submitted'.

questions.question: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error: She is one of the (A) / most talented singer (B) / in the choir (C) / of our college. (D)
questions.subject: Error Identification
questions.explanation: After 'one of the', a plural noun is required: it should be 'most talented singers'.

questions.question: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error: The number of applicants (A) / are increasing (B) / every year (C) / in this field. (D)
questions.subject: Error Identification
questions.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb, so 'are increasing' should be 'is increasing'.

questions.question: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error: He explained the concept (A) / so clearly that (B) / even the weakest student (C) / could understood it. (D)
questions.subject: Error Identification
questions.explanation: After the modal 'could', the base verb is required: 'could understand it'.

questions.question: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error: Neither of the two brothers (A) / were willing (B) / to accept (C) / the responsibility. (D)
questions.subject: Error Identification
questions.explanation: 'Neither of' takes a singular verb, so 'were willing' should be 'was willing'.

questions.question: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error: The teacher asked the students (A) / to return back (B) / the library books (C) / before the weekend. (D)
questions.subject: Error Identification
questions.explanation: 'Return back' is redundant; 'return' alone already means to give back.

questions.question: Improve the highlighted part: The manager, along with his team members, HAVE DECIDED to work overtime.
questions.subject: Sentence Improvement
questions.explanation: The subject is 'the manager' (singular). The phrase 'along with his team members' does not change the number, so 'has decided' is correct.

questions.question: Improve the highlighted part: ONE OF MY FRIEND IS a doctor.
questions.subject: Sentence Improvement
questions.explanation: 'One of' must be followed by a plural noun, so 'one of my friends is' is correct.

questions.question: Improve the highlighted part: I have been living in this city SINCE TEN YEARS.
questions.subject: Sentence Improvement
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a period of time; 'since' is used with a point in time. So 'for ten years' is correct.

questions.question: Improve the highlighted part: He is SENIOR THAN ME by two years.
questions.subject: Sentence Improvement
questions.explanation: Latin comparatives such as 'senior' take 'to', so 'senior to me' is correct.

questions.question: Improve the highlighted part: This is THE MOST UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY of my career.
questions.subject: Sentence Improvement
questions.explanation: 'Unique' is an absolute adjective and cannot take 'most', so 'a unique opportunity' is correct.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: She is good ___ mathematics.
questions.subject: Prepositions
questions.explanation: The phrase 'good at' is used for skills and subjects.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: He has been suffering ___ fever since Monday.
questions.subject: Prepositions
questions.explanation: 'Suffer from' is used for illnesses.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: Divide the sweets ___ the four children.
questions.subject: Prepositions
questions.explanation: 'Among' is used when sharing between more than two people; 'between' is used for two.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: I am looking forward ___ meeting you.
questions.subject: Prepositions
questions.explanation: 'Look forward to' is a fixed expression followed by a gerund.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: He insisted ___ paying the bill.
questions.subject: Prepositions
questions.explanation: 'Insist on' is the correct prepositional verb.

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the most appropriate word: The committee could not reach a decision because the members were ___ on the issue.
questions.subject: Fill in the Blanks
questions.explanation: 'Divided on an issue' means having opposing opinions, which explains why no decision was reached.

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the most appropriate word: Despite the heavy rain, the team ___ to complete the project on time.
questions.subject: Fill in the Blanks
questions.explanation: 'Managed to' means succeeded in doing something, which suits the contrast with the heavy rain.

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the most appropriate word: Her explanation was so ___ that everyone understood the concept immediately.
questions.subject: Fill in the Blanks
questions.explanation: 'Lucid' means clear and easy to understand, matching the idea that everyone understood immediately.

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the most appropriate word: Hard work and dedication are ___ for success in any field.
questions.subject: Fill in the Blanks
questions.explanation: 'Essential' means absolutely necessary, which fits the sense of the sentence.

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the most appropriate word: The new policy is expected to ___ the burden on small businesses.
questions.subject: Fill in the Blanks
questions.explanation: 'Reduce the burden' is the natural collocation expected of a supportive new policy.

questions.question: Passage: Urbanisation has transformed the way people live and work. While cities offer better employment, education and healthcare, they also place enormous pressure on housing, transport and the environment. Rapid migration from rural areas often outpaces a city's ability to build infrastructure, leading to congestion and pollution. Planners argue that sustainable urban development requires a balance between economic growth and quality of life. Green spaces, efficient public transport and affordable housing are no longer luxuries but necessities for the modern city. Question: According to the passage, what is the main challenge faced by rapidly growing cities?
questions.option2: Infrastructure failing to keep pace with migration
questions.answer: Infrastructure failing to keep pace with migration
questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.explanation: The passage states that rapid migration often outpaces a city's ability to build infrastructure, leading to congestion and pollution.

questions.question: Passage: Reading is one of the most effective ways to build a strong vocabulary. Regular readers encounter words in context, which helps them understand subtle shades of meaning that a dictionary alone cannot provide. However, reading passively without reflecting on new words offers limited benefit. Learners who note down unfamiliar words and use them in their own sentences retain them far better. Thus, active engagement, not mere exposure, is the key to vocabulary growth. Question: What is the central idea of the passage?
questions.option1: A dictionary is the best way to build vocabulary
questions.option2: Passive reading is enough to learn new words
questions.option3: Active engagement, not mere exposure, builds vocabulary
questions.option4: Vocabulary cannot be improved by reading
questions.answer: Active engagement, not mere exposure, builds vocabulary
questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.explanation: The concluding line states that 'active engagement, not mere exposure, is the key to vocabulary growth'.

questions.question: Arrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph and choose the correct order. (1) It provides clean energy. (2) Solar power has many advantages. (3) It also reduces electricity bills. (4) Therefore, many households are adopting it.
questions.subject: Para Jumbles
questions.explanation: (2) introduces the topic, (1) and (3) give advantages, and (4) concludes with the result.

questions.question: Arrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph and choose the correct order. (1) The team worked day and night. (2) Finally, the project was completed on time. (3) It was an important deadline. (4) As a result, the client was satisfied.
questions.subject: Para Jumbles
questions.explanation: (3) sets the context, (1) describes the effort, (2) gives the outcome, and (4) states the consequence.

questions.question: Arrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph and choose the correct order. (1) He practised every day. (2) Ravi dreamt of winning the marathon. (3) His hard work paid off. (4) He won the gold medal.
questions.subject: Para Jumbles
questions.explanation: (2) introduces the goal, (1) the action, (3) the reward of effort, and (4) the final result.

questions.question: Arrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph and choose the correct order. (1) This has led to a rise in online learning. (2) The internet has changed education. (3) Students can now learn from anywhere. (4) It has made knowledge more accessible.
questions.subject: Para Jumbles
questions.explanation: (2) states the main idea, (4) explains the effect, (3) gives a concrete example, and (1) concludes with the result.

questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
questions.option3: Where are you going, she asked?
questions.subject: Grammar
questions.explanation: The question mark stays inside the quotation marks and the reporting clause 'she asked' begins with a lowercase letter.

questions.question: Select the sentence with the correct subject-verb agreement.
questions.option1: Neither of the answers are correct.
questions.option2: Neither of the answers is correct.
questions.option3: Neither of the answer is correct.
questions.option4: Neither of the answers were correct.
questions.answer: Neither of the answers is correct.
questions.subject: Grammar
questions.explanation: 'Neither of' is singular and takes the singular verb 'is'.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive form of: The chef prepared a delicious meal.
questions.option1: A delicious meal was prepared by the chef.
questions.option2: A delicious meal is prepared by the chef.
questions.option3: A delicious meal has prepared by the chef.
questions.option4: A delicious meal were prepared by the chef.
questions.answer: A delicious meal was prepared by the chef.
questions.subject: Grammar
questions.explanation: The simple past active 'prepared' becomes 'was/were + past participle' in the passive, i.e. 'was prepared'.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that uses the correct tense.
questions.option1: She has completed her homework yesterday.
questions.option3: She is completing her homework yesterday.
questions.subject: Grammar
questions.explanation: A finished action with a definite past time marker ('yesterday') takes the simple past tense.

questions.question: You are given a positive integer N. Write a program to find the sum of all its digits.
questions.subject: Number manipulation
questions.explanation: Repeatedly take the last digit using N % 10, add it to a running total, then remove it using N // 10 until N becomes 0.
questions.inputFormat: A single line containing the integer N.
questions.outputFormat: Print a single integer: the sum of the digits of N.

questions.question: You are given a string S that contains no spaces. Write a program to print the string in reverse order.
questions.subject: Strings
questions.explanation: Read the string and print its characters from the last index down to the first index.
questions.inputFormat: A single line containing the string S.
questions.outputFormat: Print the reversed string.

questions.question: You are given an integer N. Write a program to determine whether N is a prime number. A prime number has exactly two distinct factors: 1 and itself.
questions.subject: Number manipulation
questions.explanation: If N < 2 it is not prime. Otherwise test divisors from 2 up to the square root of N; if any divides N exactly, N is not prime.
questions.inputFormat: A single line containing the integer N.
questions.outputFormat: Print YES if N is prime, otherwise print NO.

questions.question: You are given an array of N integers. Write a program to find the second largest distinct element in the array. If there is no such element, print NA.
questions.subject: Arrays
questions.explanation: Track the largest and the second largest distinct values in one pass. The second largest must be strictly smaller than the largest.
questions.problemTitle: Second Largest Element in an Array
questions.inputFormat: The first line contains N. The second line contains N space-separated integers.
questions.outputFormat: Print the second largest distinct value, or NA if it does not exist.

questions.question: You are given an R x C matrix of integers. Write a program to print its transpose. The transpose of an R x C matrix is a C x R matrix where rows become columns.
questions.subject: Matrices
questions.explanation: Read the matrix into a 2D array and print it column by column: for each column index, print the elements from every row.
questions.inputFormat: The first line contains R and C. The next R lines each contain C space-separated integers.
questions.outputFormat: Print C lines, each containing R space-separated integers forming the transpose.

questions.question: The Fibonacci sequence is defined with F(1) = 0, F(2) = 1 and F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2) for n > 2. You are given N; write a program to print the Nth Fibonacci number.
questions.subject: Recursion
questions.explanation: The sequence is 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ... Starting from 0 and 1, add the last two values repeatedly until you reach the Nth term.
questions.inputFormat: A single line containing the integer N.
questions.outputFormat: Print a single integer: the Nth Fibonacci number.

questions.question: You are given a string consisting only of the characters ( ) [ ] { }. Write a program to determine whether the brackets are balanced. Brackets are balanced if every opening bracket is closed by the matching type of bracket in the correct order.
questions.subject: Basic data structures
questions.explanation: Use a stack. Push every opening bracket. On a closing bracket, check that the stack is not empty and that the top matches the corresponding opening bracket, then pop. The string is balanced if the stack is empty at the end.
questions.inputFormat: A single line containing the bracket string S.
questions.outputFormat: Print YES if the brackets are balanced, otherwise print NO.

questions.question:
What value is printed?

SET total = 0
FOR i = 1 TO 5
    IF i MOD 2 = 1
        total = total + i
    END IF
END FOR
PRINT total
questions.subject: Pseudocode
questions.explanation: The loop adds only odd values: 1 + 3 + 5 = 9.

questions.question:
What is printed?

SET x = 3
FOR i = 1 TO 3
    x = x * 2 - i
END FOR
PRINT x
questions.subject: Pseudocode
questions.explanation: Trace: x becomes 5, then 8, then 13.

questions.question: A function scans an array once, updating a maximum value. Which statement best describes its time complexity and extra space?
questions.option1: O(n) time and O(1) extra space
questions.option2: O(log n) time and O(n) extra space
questions.option3: O(n²) time and O(1) extra space
questions.option4: O(1) time and O(n) extra space
questions.answer: O(n) time and O(1) extra space
questions.subject: Programming Fundamentals
questions.explanation: Each of n elements is inspected once, and only a fixed number of variables are stored.

questions.question: A subclass overrides a method. A base-class reference points to a subclass object, and the method is called. Which implementation runs in a typical object-oriented language with dynamic dispatch?
questions.subject: OOP
questions.explanation: Dynamic dispatch chooses the overridden implementation based on the runtime object type.

questions.question: A report must include departments with at least five employees. Which SQL clause filters groups after COUNT(*) is computed?
questions.subject: DBMS
questions.explanation: HAVING filters grouped rows after aggregation; WHERE filters individual rows before grouping.

questions.question: Given Orders(order_id, customer_id, amount), which query returns each customer with total spending above 1000?
questions.option1: SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) FROM Orders WHERE SUM(amount)>1000 GROUP BY customer_id;
questions.option2: SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) FROM Orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(amount)>1000;
questions.option3: SELECT customer_id FROM Orders HAVING amount>1000;
questions.option4: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM Orders ORDER BY customer_id>1000;
questions.answer: SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) FROM Orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(amount)>1000;
questions.subject: SQL
questions.explanation: The query groups orders by customer, computes each total, then filters groups with HAVING.

questions.question: Two threads increment the same counter without synchronization. The final value is sometimes lower than expected. What is the most likely cause?
questions.option1: A race condition on the shared update
questions.answer: A race condition on the shared update
questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.explanation: The read-modify-write operation can interleave across threads, causing updates to be lost.

questions.question: A client needs reliable, ordered delivery for a file transfer. Which transport protocol is the best fit?
questions.option2: TCP because it provides ordered reliable delivery
questions.answer: TCP because it provides ordered reliable delivery
questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.explanation: TCP provides sequence tracking, retransmission and ordered byte-stream delivery.

questions.question: A team wants managed runtime and deployment tools while retaining control of its application code, but not the underlying servers. Which service model fits best?
questions.subject: Cloud Computing
questions.explanation: Platform as a Service provides a managed application platform while the customer deploys and manages its code.

questions.question: A database stores password verifiers. Which approach is most appropriate?
questions.option1: Store reversible encryption keys beside each password
questions.option2: Store salted, slow password hashes using a password-hashing function
questions.option3: Store passwords as plain text behind a firewall
questions.answer: Store salted, slow password hashes using a password-hashing function
questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.explanation: A unique salt and a deliberately slow password-hashing function make offline guessing harder; encoding is not protection.

questions.question: A defect appears only when two requests update the same account at once. Which test is most likely to reproduce it?
questions.option1: A concurrency test with overlapping updates
questions.answer: A concurrency test with overlapping updates
questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.explanation: The suspected behavior depends on concurrent interleaving, so overlapping requests are needed to reproduce it.

questions.question: A colleague asks for a status update, but you are still investigating a blocker. Which response is clearest?
questions.option1: Say the work is complete to avoid concern
questions.option2: State what is complete, describe the blocker, and give a time for the next update
questions.option3: Wait until the colleague asks again
questions.answer: State what is complete, describe the blocker, and give a time for the next update
questions.subject: Communication
questions.explanation: A useful update is candid, specific about impact, and includes a concrete next communication point.

questions.question: Choose the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement.
questions.option1: The list of pending tasks are attached.
questions.option2: The list of pending tasks is attached.
questions.option3: The list of pending tasks were attached.
questions.option4: The list of pending tasks have attached.
questions.answer: The list of pending tasks is attached.
questions.subject: Communication
questions.explanation: The subject is “list,” which is singular; “of pending tasks” is a modifying phrase.

questions.question: A client requests a change that may affect the agreed deadline. What is the best first response?
questions.option1: Promise the deadline will not change before assessing the work
questions.option2: Clarify the requested scope, assess the impact, and confirm a revised plan
questions.option4: Make the change silently and skip testing
questions.answer: Clarify the requested scope, assess the impact, and confirm a revised plan
questions.subject: Communication
questions.explanation: Clarifying scope and communicating impact supports a reliable commitment.

questions.question: In a project update, “mitigate the risk” most nearly means:
questions.option2: Reduce the likelihood or impact of the risk
questions.option3: Transfer every task to a different team
questions.answer: Reduce the likelihood or impact of the risk
questions.subject: Communication
questions.explanation: To mitigate is to make a problem or its consequences less severe.

questions.question: Given an array of N integers (possibly negative), find the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray. The subarray must contain at least one element.
questions.option1: Write your solution in the editor above.
questions.answer: Write your solution in the editor above.
questions.subject: Arrays
questions.explanation: The subarray [4, -1, 2, 1] has the maximum sum = 6. Kadane's algorithm tracks a running max.
questions.inputFormat:
First line contains a single integer N.
Second line contains N space-separated integers.
questions.outputFormat: Print a single integer — the maximum subarray sum.

questions.question: Given an array of N integers and a number K, rotate the array to the right by K positions. Rotation wraps elements from the end back to the beginning.
questions.option1: Write your solution in the editor above.
questions.answer: Write your solution in the editor above.
questions.subject: Arrays
questions.explanation: After rotating right by 2: [4,5,1,2,3]. Effective rotation = K mod N = 2.
questions.inputFormat:
First line contains two integers N and K.

questions.question: Given an array A of N integers, perform at most K operations. In each operation, select a contiguous subarray and add its sum to your score, then replace all its elements with 0. questions.answer: Write your solution in the editor above.
questions.subject: Prefix sums
questions.explanation: Op1: pick [3,-1,4,-1,5]=10, array=[0,0,0,0,0]. Op2: pick anything=0. Total=10. Wait, better: Op1: [4,-1,5]=8, then Op2:[3,-1]=2. Total=10. Or Op1: [3,-1,4,-1,5]=10. Score=10. Actually whole array = 10. Could do [4,5]=9 then [3]=3=12? No: [4,-1,5]=8, rest [3,-1]=2, 8+2=10. Best is [3,-1,4,-1,5]=10 in one shot, 0 remaining. OR split: take [5]=5 first, then [3,-1,4,-1]=5, total=10. Best=11: take [4,5]=9+[3]=3? Wait: [4,-1,5]=8, not [4,5]. Array: indices 0-4: 3,-1,4,-1,5. [4,5] is non-contiguous. Must be contiguous. Best: subarray [3,-1,4,-1,5]=10. Or [4,-1,5]=8 then [3]=3... no [3] and [-1] surround. [3] alone=3, score=3+8=11. Yes! Take subarray [0..0]=3 (score=3), array becomes [0,-1,4,-1,5]. Then take [2..4]=4-1+5=8 (score=11). Total=11.
